title: useState basics
summary: useState stores component data that can change over time and trigger a re-render.
whenToUse: Use it for local UI data such as counters, selected tabs, form fields, toggles, and small component state.
do: Call useState at the top level of a component.
Use the setter function to update state.
Use a functional update when the next value depends on the previous value.
dont: Do not mutate state variables directly.
Do not call hooks inside conditions, loops, or nested functions.

title: Event handlers
summary: Event handlers are functions React runs in response to user actions.
whenToUse: Use handlers for clicks, form changes, submits, keyboard events, and other user interactions.
do: Pass a function reference to event props.
Name handlers after the action they handle, like handleSubmit.
Keep handler logic short or move complex logic into helper functions.
dont: Do not call the handler while rendering unless you intentionally return another function.
Do not rely on stale state when the next value depends on the previous value.

commonMistake: Calling the handler during render with onClick={handleClick()} instead of passing the function.
interviewQuestion: Why do we pass a function to onClick instead of calling it?
interviewAnswer: Passing a function lets React call it later when the event happens; calling it runs immediately during render.

title: Controlled inputs
summary: A controlled input gets its value from React state and updates that state on change.
whenToUse: Use controlled inputs when React needs to validate, submit, reset, or react to form values.
do: Store the input value in state.
Use the state value when submitting or validating the form.
dont: Do not pass value without an onChange handler unless the field is intentionally read-only.
Do not read directly from the DOM when React state already owns the form value.

codeSnippets.title: Controlled text input
codeSnippets.description: State is the source of truth for the input value.
codeSnippets.explanation: Every keystroke updates state, and the input displays the current state value.

codeSnippets.title: Use the value on submit
codeSnippets.description: Controlled state is ready to use when the form submits.
codeSnippets.explanation: The submit handler can use the latest state value without querying the DOM.

commonMistake: Providing a value prop without an onChange handler, which makes the input read-only.
interviewQuestion: What makes an input controlled in React?
interviewAnswer: Its displayed value comes from React state, and every change updates that state through an event handler.

courseReference.notes: Form fields are a practical place to connect input values to component state.
